item.title: Dad's Daily Digest — 2026-03-10
item.description:
# Episode Summary
This episode breaks down a dramatic 24-hour period in markets triggered by geopolitical tension with Iran, featuring wild swings in oil prices and stocks before rebounding on reports that the conflict could end soon. Beyond the markets, the discussion covers the succession of Iran's new Supreme Leader and the humanitarian toll of the conflict, including damage to critical water infrastructure amid an existing crisis. The episode also examines how rising energy prices complicate the administration's midterm agenda and explores China's strategic positioning through aggressive oil stockpiling ahead of the conflict.

item.title: Dad's Daily Digest — 2026-03-07
item.description:
# Episode Summary
This episode examines the escalating Iran conflict and its cascading effects on global markets and everyday costs—from a historic 14% weekly spike in gas prices to ripple effects on food production through disrupted fertilizer supplies and higher shipping costs. The discussion explores geopolitical complexities including the emerging role of low-cost drone warfare, Europe's particular vulnerability to energy shocks, and the intraday market volatility that's creating investor anxiety this week. A featured analysis argues that dividend-focused investing offers a grounding perspective during uncertain times by shifting focus from daily price swings to steady cash flow generation.

item.title: Dad's Daily Digest — 2026-03-06
item.description:
# Episode Summary
This episode covers four major stories shaping the week: gas prices spiking 11% to an 18-month high due to Iran conflict fallout, turbulent global markets absorbing geopolitical uncertainty and Fed policy concerns, and the surprise firing of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem amid ongoing crises. The discussion connects abstract geopolitics to concrete economic impacts—from what Americans pay at the pump to questions about data reliability influencing Fed decisions—while examining ripple effects across the Middle East, Europe, and consumer spending.

item.title: Dad's Daily Digest — 2026-03-05
item.description:
# Thursday Morning Briefing
This episode breaks down three major stories reshaping the economic and political landscape: an escalating Iran conflict with no clear resolution that's threatening energy prices, supply chains, and government finances—forcing the Federal Reserve into an even tighter corner; a new "no tax on overtime" policy with appealing headlines but complicated real-world implementation that could catch workers off guard at tax time; and a Texas Republican Senate runoff on May 26th that signals which faction of the party is gaining control heading into the midterm cycle. Along the way, the hosts also examine the underreported crisis of child care costs rising faster than inflation, quietly straining American households and workforce participation.

item.title: Dad's Daily Digest — 2026-03-03
item.description:
# Tuesday News Digest
This episode digs into three major storylines reshaping markets and business this week: escalating Iran conflict is pushing global markets into uncertainty, with energy prices and inflation now the primary concern rather than recession risk. Domestically, small businesses are caught in tariff chaos—facing unclear refund processes for struck-down tariffs and impossible pricing decisions amid constant policy shifts. Finally, legacy automakers face an urgent reckoning on whether to fully commit to EVs and autonomous vehicles or risk obsolescence as Chinese competitors and tech companies accelerate their own transitions.

item.title: Dad's Daily Digest — 2026-03-02
item.description:
# Episode Summary
This episode breaks down the escalating Iran conflict and its far-reaching consequences across global markets, energy security, and geopolitics. Key topics include oil price pressures and disruption threats to the Strait of Hormuz, Europe's vulnerability as a sidelined ally, and Asia's precarious position facing simultaneous trade war and energy shock headwinds. The discussion also covers domestic political leverage being applied to the Iran situation, Fed inflation concerns, and broader market uncertainty as equities grapple with stretched valuations amid geopolitical risk.

item.title: Dad's Daily Digest — 2026-03-01

This episode covers the geopolitical earthquake following Iran's Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei's assassination—including newly revealed CIA involvement in the Israeli operation and how it disrupts energy markets through potential Strait of Hormuz disruptions—alongside analysis of Berkshire Hathaway's post-Buffett transition under new CEO Gregory Abel, whose corporate communication style signals a genuine shift in the company's era. The episode also examines the rising sophistication of workplace surveillance software and its counterproductive effects on employee trust and retention.
